prompt: Introduce a charge of 12 credits on private vehicles entering the central business district between 7am and 7pm on weekdays, starting 2026-01-01. Exempt buses, taxis, and blue-badge holders. Spend 70% of the revenue on public transport and 20% on cycling and walking. The aim is to cut congestion and emissions without raising costs for low-income residents by more than 5%.

failure_modes.risk: Transit overcrowding during the adaptation gap
failure_modes.mechanism: Behavioural mode shift overwhelms transit at month 1, but the revenue-funded capacity ramp only lands at month 12 — early riders get the worst service.

evidence.detail: Peak CBD-bound transit demand exceeds baseline capacity (1823 vs ~1447 trips/day headroom). (month 1, conf 0.9)
Revenue-funded transit capacity ramp lands: boardings up 8% vs the short-run level as cheaper/faster service pulls more commuters onto transit. (month 12, conf 0.85)

failure_modes.mitigation: Phase the charge in (or pre-fund bus capacity before day one) so service headroom leads demand rather than lagging it.

failure_modes.mechanism: Every projected benefit is conditional on the assumed price/time elasticities and reinvestment pace; the confidence bands widen monotonically to the 10-year horizon precisely because those inputs are uncertain.
failure_modes.mitigation: Run the uncertainty sweep over key elasticities and monitor the early-months outturn against the modelled path; be ready to retune.

failure_modes.risk: Charge revenue erodes as drivers leave
failure_modes.mechanism: The same -17.5-pt car-share fall that makes the policy work also shrinks the priced base funding the transit uplift, so the mid-run reinvestment it depends on is self-limiting.
failure_modes.mitigation: Plan for a declining revenue path: front-load capacity investment and diversify the transit funding base beyond the charge.

analogues.note: Historical Analogue / Causal Layer (SPEC §7.1): estimates the flagship cordon-traffic effect from comparable real-world schemes via a difference-in-differences read (treated change − background trend) transferred to this policy by an auditable similarity score. Historical outcomes are Observed but illustrative/approximate published figures, not this city's microdata; the transferred estimate is Estimated. No LLM touches any number (SPEC §7.1/§34).

stress.note: Each named shock is a transparent scenario assumption applied to BOTH worlds, so Δ(B−A) still isolates the policy. A scenario 'fails' when the policy's benefit on a headline metric is neutralised or reversed relative to the no-shock baseline (SPEC §20).

sdg.note: SDG alignment maps deterministic simulation + cohort-opinion outcomes onto UN SDG targets via measurable indicators / transparent proxies. economy.note: Transparent input-output / elasticity translation of the deterministic mode-choice simulation into local-economy channels (SPEC §7.4). Physical drivers (mode shifts, charge revenue, travel-cost changes) are Simulated; the monetary translation is Estimated. Partial-equilibrium only — no CGE, no agglomeration/land-value effects. No LLM produced any number (SPEC §34).

channels.name: Cordon charge withdrawn from household spending
channels.mechanism: Charge revenue is money moved out of charged commuters' discretionary budgets; the locally-spent fraction leaves local demand until it is recycled (see revenue recycling).
channels.note: A transfer, not a deadweight loss — recycled by the next channel.

channels.name: Recycled revenue re-spent locally (transit + fund)
channels.mechanism: All revenue collected at the cordon and allocated to public transport and the general fund is re-spent — labour-intensive transit operations and capital — circulating through the local economy at a fiscal multiplier.
channels.physical_basis: annual cordon charge revenue (commuter Simulated + freight Estimated)
channels.note: Net of the withdrawal and freight channels, reinvestment typically makes the charge locally positive.

channels.name: CBD retail & hospitality footfall
channels.mechanism: Commuting is conserved (mode shift, not trip loss), so worker footfall holds; a small share of deterred car trips is foregone entirely, while pedestrianisation raises retail amenity and dwell-time spend.
channels.physical_basis: Δ CBD-bound car commuters (Simulated); shopper demand not agent-modelled
channels.note: Sign is genuinely uncertain: pedestrianisation tends positive, a pure charge slightly negative. Discretionary shopper response is NOT modelled.

channels.name: Freight & delivery charge passed to CBD business
channels.mechanism: Delivery/freight vehicles entering the cordon pay the charge; most of that cost is passed through to central businesses and their customers.
channels.physical_basis: baseline CBD vehicle entries × freight share (Estimated — freight not in the synthetic population)
channels.note: Low confidence: freight demand is a documented ratio, not agent-modelled.

channels.name: Commuter mode-switch travel-time cost
channels.mechanism: Commuters who switch mode to avoid the charge/ban spend more (or less) time travelling; that time is valued at the model's value of time.
channels.physical_basis: Σ Δ commuter travel-minutes/year from mode switches (Simulated)
channels.note: Value of time ≈ 0.125/min, the inverse of the GC model's money↔time conversion (consistent with the mode-choice model). Excludes the charge money itself (counted in the transfer channel).

sector_exposure.mechanism: Footfall held by conserved commuting; pedestrian amenity up, car-avoidance down.
Reinvested revenue funds service operations and staffing.
Capital share of transit reinvestment supports short-run construction activity.
Cordon charge raises delivery costs into the centre.
Commuters bear mode-switch travel-time costs and the charge, partly offset by faster/cheaper transit from reinvestment.

not_modelled: Congestion-relief time savings for remaining traffic — link speeds are fixed in this MVP; would require the spatial traffic-assignment layer (SPEC §7.7).
Agglomeration, land-value and rent effects of improved central accessibility.
Discretionary (non-commuter) shopper and tourist demand response.
Wage / labour-market general equilibrium (this is partial-equilibrium only).

Crowding-out / opportunity cost of the fiscal multiplier — recycled revenue is credited at a local multiplier without netting the alternative use of that money, so the net sign is sensitive to the multiplier assumption (Estimated).
